reason: The sources provide over 15 consistent claims across multiple sites, including the mission's near-failure, recovery, and unexpected record-breaking comet discoveries.
story: SOHO was built to stare at the Sun, not find space rocks. Launched in 1995 for a two-year mission, the joint ESA/NASA satellite was nearly lost in 1998 when a command error sent it into a terrifying uncontrolled spin. For months, it drifted silent and frozen in space. Engineers eventually pulled off a miracle recovery, even inventing a way to steer the spacecraft without its failed gyroscopes by using reaction wheels as virtual ones. But the real twist? By using its LASCO instrument to block out the Sun's glare, SOHO accidentally became the most prolific comet hunter in history. It has spotted over 5,000 comets—more than half of all known comets ever recorded. Most weren't found by professionals, but by citizen scientists combing through public data from their homes. From a near-death experience to an unexpected legacy of discovery, SOHO is still going strong 30 years later.
angle: A satellite designed to study the Sun for just two years survived a mission-ending blackout to accidentally discover over 5,000 comets—more than half of all comets known to humanity.

claims.claim: The mission is a joint project between the European Space Agency (ESA) and NASA.
SOHO is located in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point.
The spacecraft is positioned approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
The mission was originally planned to last for only two years.
Contact with SOHO was lost in June 1998 after a command error caused an uncontrolled spin.
Engineers recovered the spacecraft after it spent months silent and frozen in space.
All of SOHO's stabilizing gyroscopes eventually failed.
SOHO became the first three-axis-stabilized spacecraft to use its reaction wheels as virtual gyroscopes.
The LASCO instrument uses a disc to block the Sun's glare, creating an artificial eclipse.
This masking of the Sun's direct light allows SOHO to see the surrounding corona and nearby comets.
SOHO discovered its 5,000th comet in March 2024.
SOHO has discovered more than half of all known comets.
Approximately 95 percent of SOHO's comet discoveries have been made by citizen scientists.
The 5,000th comet was found by Hanjie Tan, a PhD student from Prague.
SOHO monitors coronal mass ejections to provide early warnings of solar storms reaching Earth.
SOHO has observed nearly three full 11-year solar cycles.

disputed: The exact length of the 1998 blackout period varies by source, with accounts ranging from three months (S6) to four months (S2); the script should attribute this as 'several months' or 'about three months.'

The specific count of total comets discovered is updated at different times across sources (e.g., 5,217 in S1 vs 5,204 in S7); the script should use 'over 5,000' to remain accurate across all sources.
